Lemma
[the star boundary of $\operatorname {seg}(p)$] Source: petersen:page-0235 ↗ lem:pet-ch5-exp-nonsingular-segment-domain ↗ rem:pet-ch5-segment-domain-chart-artifact

1. ch5:5.7.9

If $v\in \operatorname {seg}(p)-\operatorname {seg}^0(p)$, then either (1) there is $w e v$ in $\operatorname {seg}(p)$ with $\exp _p(v)=\exp _p(w)$, or (2) $D\exp _p$ is singular at $v$.

Formalization status. Not formalized, and it cannot be formalized against the on-disk definitions as they stand: read there, the statement is false rather than merely unproven, because segmentDomain inherits the chart artifact of the on-disk exponential. See subsection 7.3. The lemma as stated above — at the intrinsic exponential, which is Petersen's — is the true statement and is what a formalization should target.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch5-cut-locus-characterization \sketch For $t_n\downarrow 1$, choose minimizing segments to $\exp _p(t_nv)$ and take a convergent subsequence of their initial vectors, with limit $w$ and $|w|=|v|$. If $w e v$, then $\exp _pw=\exp _pv$, giving (1). If $w=v$ and $D\exp _p|_v$ were nonsingular, local injectivity would identify the nearby initial vectors with $t_nv$, making the radial geodesic minimizing beyond $v$. This contradicts $v otin \operatorname {seg}^0(p)$, so case (2) holds.

□
